title: helm: private values schema + init/upgrade/rollback hooks and templating polish
author: Elena Park
description: Motivation: Harden the Redwood Private Helm chart for safer installs, upgrades, and rollbacks in VPC/on-prem environments. This change improves the values schema, tightens templating around optional components (KMS, extraSecrets, initContainers), adds explicit init/upgrade/rollback hook Jobs to ensure deterministic migration and credential initialization, and includes Chart-level metadata and test coverage for the hooks. Scope: values.schema.json and values.yaml updates to express KMS and migration flags, templates/init-job.yaml, templates/upgrade-hook.yaml, templates/rollback-hook.yaml, helper template fixes for conditional rendering, NOTES.txt updates and test cases under tests/. This PR is intended to reduce manual post-install steps customers perform in Private deployments and to make automatic rollbacks less error-prone by cleaning up stale state. The description below summarizes changes, reasoning, and rollout considerations. Changes: 1) Values schema: expanded values.schema.json with JSON Schema validation for kms.provider (aws|gcp|azure|vault|none), kms.keyRef, migration.enable boolean, migration.mode (validate|apply), hooks.enabled boolean, tls. This catches common misconfigurations before helm install/upgrade and reduces operator errors. 2) Templating: updated _helpers.tpl to centralize conditional rendering for kms, extraSecrets, and persistence. Deployment templates now use include "redwood.fullname" and consistent labels to avoid drift. 3) Init job: templates/init-job.yaml is a post-install hook job that runs once to bootstrap admin keys, ensure DB schema version record exists, optionally write initial secrets to the configured KMS provider, and set a ConfigMap flag used by the main Deployment to skip first-run migrations. The job uses ttlSecondsAfterFinished to avoid leaving jobs forever and uses backoffLimit with clear logs. 4) Upgrade hook: templates/upgrade-hook.yaml is annotated as an helm pre-upgrade hook with weight 100 to run before new pods are rolled; it validates current schema versions and, when migration.mode=apply, runs safe DB migrations inside a Job. The hook runs with a short timeout and emits a MigrationStatus CR (optional) if CRDs present. 5) Rollback hook: templates/rollback-hook.yaml ensures transient resources created during a failed upgrade are cleaned up and that a safe fallback config (pinned model version or feature toggle) is restored from a stored ConfigMap. Annotated as pre-rollback and uses a conservative TTL to allow operator inspection. 6) CRD and RBAC: added minimal RBAC roles required by hook Jobs (get/configmap/secrets, update CRs if CRDs enabled) and a note in README about granting the installer service account these permissions in air-gapped installs. 7) Tests and CI: added helm unittest test files under tests/ for the init and upgrade hooks, and added a chart rendering sanity job to CI. 8) Chart metadata: bumped Chart.yaml version and appVersion, updated NOTES.txt with manual fallback steps and a short troubleshooting checklist. Rollout plan and backward compatibility: the schema additions are additive; existing installs will still render since default values are set to preserve previous behavior. Operators are recommended to run helm lint --strict and the included unit tests before applying to production. For customers using older helm clients, notes include a compatibility matrix. How this was validated: local helm template/render on k8s 1.24 and 1.27 clusters, helm unittest pass on dry-run, manual smoke test of init job on a staging Private cluster using local KMS emulator. See CI checks for automated results. Docs and follow-ups: updated README and NOTES.txt, and added a Linear link for follow-up to add CR-backed migration reporting and a small feature to expose hook logs in the Console (ENG-1297).

Author (Elena Park): Default set to validate; migration.mode=apply must be explicitly enabled in values.

release_notes: Enhancements: Helm chart now includes validated values schema for KMS and migration flags, init/upgrade/rollback hook Jobs to ensure deterministic bootstrap and migration workflows, RBAC notes for air-gapped installers, and CI tests for hooks. Backwards-compatible defaults preserve existing installs. Operators: review migration.mode before upgrading and run tests in staging.
tests: ci: chart-render job on kube-1.24 and kube-1.27
notes: This PR intentionally keeps schema additions additive. Administrators with managed KMS should set kms.provider and kms.keyRef before enabling migration.mode=apply. For dedicated/private installs, ensure the installer SA has permissions to get/update ConfigMaps and Secrets. See NOTES.txt for quick rollback commands. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-1297 to expose hook logs in Console.
